prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: Building on c013 (timing-driven weighting + decay<=0.5 + max_net_weight=8, score +0.619), the per-region density update currently inflates the density penalty up to a hard clamp of 5 and keeps growing the step size; capping the per-region density weight at a lower ceiling (3.5) and slowing the step-size growth further (1.015/1.025) reduces over-spreading in already-nearly-legal regions, shortening critical wires and giving rsz more room, which should reduce TNS across all circuits.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.136 robust(mean-std)=+0.031 min_case=+0.027 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.062 dWNS=+6.6% dTNS=+6.3% overflow~69
  bp-ng45: score=+0.027 dWNS=-0.5% dTNS=+4.9% overflow~136
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.047 dWNS=-2.0% dTNS=+8.9% overflow~117
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Hypothesis held: all three cases improved TNS (ariane +6.3%, bp +4.9%, bp_fe +8.9%), with robust mean-std +0.031 and all_valid. WNS gains are mixed (ariane +6.6%, bp -0.5%, bp_fe -2.0%), suggesting the lower density ceiling (3.5) and slower step growth (1.015/1.025) reduce over-spreading, shortening critical wires and freeing rsz—most visible where overflow is high (bp_fe ~117). Next step: sweep the density ceiling (3.0/3.5/4.0) at fixed step growth to isolate which lever drives the TNS gain and check WNS regressions on bp/bp_fe.
